body:
minor nit, but i'd suggest rewording this to say "...a checkbox with a checked, unchecked and indeterminate state."

while obviously similar, this difference (on/off vs checked/unchecked) also shows it's not just that switch removes the indeterminate state, but that the actual _state_ becomes on/off rather than checked/unchecked.  outside of the exposed role, these changes in state are generally how they're exposed by screen readers.

```suggestion [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean switch; ``` …because per https://whatpr.org/html/9546/d6ce12a...0f2ec68/input.html#dom-input-switch, it is required to reflect, right? And the IDL in the WebKit sources has this: ```c++ [EnabledBySetting=SwitchControlEnabled, CEReactions=NotNeeded, Reflect] attribute boolean switch; ```
[Reflect] is not a standard IDL extended attribute; it's implementation-specific (similar to [EnabledBySetting]).
